chunks.arabic_text: أُمَيَّةُ بْنُ عَلِيٍّ، الْقَيْسِيُّ، يُكْنَى أَبَا مُحَمَّدٍ. فِي عِدَادِ الْقُمِّيِّينَ، ضَعِيفُ الرِّوَايَةِ، فِي مَذْهَبِهِ ارْتِفَاعٌ.

translations.en: Umayya ibn Ali, al-Qaysi, known by the kunya Abu Muhammad. Among the Qummi scholars, weak in narration, in his madhhab there is irtifa' (elevation/height).

en.summary: Umayya ibn Ali al-Qaysi, a narrator from Qum, is recorded in al-Ghada'iri's *Kitab al-Duafa* as having a weak hadith transmission (*da'if al-riwaya*) and a theological stance characterized by *irtifa* (elevation), which often denotes the belief in the physical ascension of the Imams or a specific doctrinal elevation distinct from mainstream Twelver Shiism. This entry highlights the nuanced evaluation of narrators not just by reliability but by their theological alignment, reflecting the scholarly concern with preserving doctrinal purity alongside textual accuracy in early Shia hadith sciences.
en.seo_question: Who is Umayya ibn Ali al-Qaysi and what is his status in Shia hadith sciences?

key_terms.ارْتِفَاعٌ: Irtifa' (elevation/height, often referring to doctrinal elevation or specific theological position)
